Bill.BriefDescription: Adjusting procedures of vessel dealer trust accounts.

BillBody.BillTitle: AN ACT Relating to vessel dealer trust accounts; and amending RCW88.02.220.
BillBody.EnactingClause: BE IT ENACTED BY THE LEGISLATURE OF THE STATE OF WASHINGTON:

BegSecAmd.BegSecText: RCW 88.02.220 and 1991 c 339 s 33 are each amended to readas follows:

BillSection.RCWSLText: A vessel dealer who receives cash or a negotiable instrument ofdeposit in excess of one thousand dollars, or a deposit of any amountthat will be held for more than fourteen calendar days, shall place thefunds in a separate trust account. (1) The cash or negotiable instrument must be set aside immediatelyupon receipt for the trust account, or endorsed to such a trust accountimmediately upon receipt. (2) The cash or negotiable instrument must be deposited in thetrust account ((by the close of banking hours on the day following thereceipt)) within fortyeight hours of acceptance of offer by seller andbuyer. The offer must be made to the seller within fortyeight hoursof receipt of the funds, or the cash or negotiable instrument must beeither returned to the buyer or deposited into the trust account. p. 1 SB 5137 (3) After delivery of the purchaser's vessel the vessel dealershall remove the deposited funds from the trust account. (4) The dealer shall ((not commingle the purchaser's funds with anyother funds at any time)) place the purchaser's funds in a separatenoninterest bearing trust account. (5) The funds shall remain in the trust account until the deliveryof the purchased vessel. However, upon written agreement from thepurchaser, the vessel dealer may remove and release trust funds beforedelivery.
